title: Ultraproducts: truth modulo an ultrafilter

based_on.title: Model Theory for Algebra and Algebraic Geometry, Orsay sections 1–3

summary: Combine structures using an ultrafilter, prove Łoś's theorem, construct a nonstandard arithmetic model, and obtain compactness for arbitrary set-sized languages.
abstract: Can sequences of elements of a structure become elements of a new model that preserves its first-order truths? An ultrafilter specifies which sets of coordinates count as large. Identifying sequences that agree on a large set gives an ultrapower, and Łoś's theorem evaluates every formula by the coordinates where it holds. The original structure embeds into this model by constant sequences. For natural-number arithmetic, a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the natural numbers gives an element outside that copy while preserving every sentence true in the usual natural numbers. Allowing the factors to be different structures gives ultraproducts and a proof of compactness for any set-sized first-order language.
